title: U.S. House · Texas's 23rd District
area: West and South Texas, stretching from San Antonio's outskirts along the border to El Paso County.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Tony Gonzales trailed Brandon Herrera in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, 41.8% to 43.3%, forcing a runoff; Gonzales withdrew before the May 26, 2026 runoff, which was canceled, and Herrera advanced. Katy Padilla Stout won the Democratic nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary. Ben Mendoza, a perennial candidate who previously ran for El Paso mayor, is on the ballot as an independent.

candidates.name: Brandon Herrera
candidates.ballotNote: Led the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 43.3% of the vote, then advanced to the general election after incumbent Tony Gonzales withdrew and the scheduled runoff was canceled.

summary.text: Brandon Herrera is the Republican nominee for this open border-area seat. He describes himself as an entrepreneur, Second Amendment activist and social media personality who started a firearms manufacturing business and built a large YouTube following. He challenged Rep. Tony Gonzales in the 2024 Republican primary runoff, losing narrowly, and advanced to the 2026 general election after Gonzales withdrew from the runoff.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he has deep Texas family roots and Hispanic heritage, and both of his parents come from military families.
Attended Campbell College, where he studied pre-law, before leaving to start a firearms manufacturing business.
According to his campaign website, he moved to Texas for good after the 2020 COVID lockdowns and brought his businesses and employees with him.

As of the 2024 election, hosted a YouTube channel focused on firearms-related content with more than 3 million subscribers; his campaign website says his content has accumulated over half a billion views.
His campaign website says he works with groups including the National Association for Gun Rights, the Firearm Policy Coalition, Gun Owners of America and Young Americans for Liberty.
Ran against incumbent Tony Gonzales in the 2024 Republican primary for this district, advancing to a runoff that Gonzales won on May 28, 2024, 50.6% to 49.4%.
Finished first in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 43.3% to Gonzales's 41.8%; Gonzales withdrew before the May 26 runoff, which was canceled, making Herrera the nominee.

candidates.name: Katy Padilla Stout
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.1% of the vote over three other candidates.

summary.text: Katy Padilla Stout is the Democratic nominee for this open border-area seat. She is an attorney and former elementary school teacher who, according to her campaign website, practices child welfare and education law at a family firm in Carrizo Springs. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.1% of the vote in a four-candidate field.

background.text: Describes herself as a lifelong Texan raised by a single mother; says her father and grandparents were migrant farmworkers from South Texas.
Graduated from Lee High School in San Antonio and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas at Austin, in education according to her campaign website.
Taught elementary school in Northside ISD before attending law school.

Earned a law degree from the South Texas College of Law and built a practice focused on child welfare and education law; she says she now works with her father at their family firm based in Carrizo Springs.

Has served since 2017 as an appointed member of the Bexar County Child Welfare Board and sits on the board of directors of Artvango Therapeutic Services, a nonprofit that provides expressive therapies for children.
Says she lives in San Antonio with her husband, a career prosecutor, and their four children, two of whom they adopted through foster care.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.1% of the vote over Santos Limon, Bruce Richardson and Gretel Marysdatter Enck.

candidates.name: Ben Mendoza

summary.text: Ben Mendoza is an independent candidate for this seat. He is an El Paso-area candidate who has run in several earlier local and federal races, most recently placing eighth in the 2024 El Paso mayoral general election. Ballotpedia lists no biographical information or campaign materials for him.

background.text: Ran as an independent in the 2018 general election for Texas's 16th Congressional District, receiving 4.5% of the vote (8,147 votes) in a race won by Veronica Escobar.
Ran in the 2019 El Paso Independent School District, District 3 election, receiving 7.1% of the vote.
Ran in the December 9, 2023 special general election for El Paso City Council District 2, receiving 4.1% of the vote.
Ran for Mayor of El Paso in 2024, finishing eighth in a field of eight candidates with 4.6% of the vote.
